index_schema_standard.estimated_token_savings: Removing derived sections (tag_index, categories, by_* lookups) saves ~3,500 tokens (~57%) from KB index.json alone. Unified field names eliminate agent confusion when switching between index files.

estimated_token_savings.index_schema_unification: ~3,500 tokens saved per KB index read by removing derived sections (tag_index, categories). Similar savings across other indexes.
estimated_token_savings.deterministic_path_resolution: ~50 tokens saved per SOP/SRC lookup by eliminating need to consult index for filename. Agents construct path from ID directly.
estimated_token_savings.naming_consistency: Reduces agent confusion and retry costs. Estimated 200-500 tokens saved per session from fewer exploratory reads.

design_decisions.no_directory_renames: All directories keep current names. The token savings from shorter paths (knowledge-base/ -> kb/) do not justify the migration cost of updating CLAUDE.md, all documentation, and all hardcoded paths. The repo is not large enough for path length to be a significant token cost.
design_decisions.id_only_filenames_for_indexed_resources: SOP and SRC files drop descriptive suffixes from filenames. This enables convention-over-configuration: knowing the ID is sufficient to construct the file path. KB and TEAM files already follow this pattern successfully.
design_decisions.keep_yaml_frontmatter: TT-Alpha suggested replacing YAML frontmatter with inline JSON headers. This is rejected because: (1) YAML frontmatter is a GitHub-standard pattern with rendering support, (2) 100% of KB entries already use it, (3) migration cost exceeds token savings, (4) YAML is more human-readable than JSON for metadata.
design_decisions.keep_json_indexes: TT-Alpha suggested .manifest (TSV) or NDJSON formats. JSON indexes are kept because: (1) they are the established pattern at 100% adoption, (2) all existing tooling (generate_registry.py, kb_validator.py) reads JSON, (3) the schema unification alone provides the majority of the token savings.
design_decisions.unified_entries_key: All indexes use 'entries' as the array key. This is a breaking change from 'tools', 'scripts', 'sources', etc. but eliminates the cognitive overhead of remembering different keys per resource type.
